subject: English
passage: Animals exhibit complex communication behaviors to share information with members of their species. Such communication serves purposes including warning of danger, establishing territory, and coordinating group activities. For many years, scientists believed that only mammals possessed sophisticated vocal communication systems. Recent research on birds and other creatures, however, has challenged the assumption that advanced communication requires mammalian vocal structures. Remarkably, prairie dogs use distinct alarm calls to identify different types of predators approaching their colonies. Honeybees also demonstrate complexity through their waggle dance, which conveys precise information about the distance and direction of food sources.
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To question the belief that insects are capable of learning
choices.B: To compare communication methods in mammals with communication methods in honeybees
choices.C: To argue that a variety of animals have sophisticated communication systems
choices.D: To establish that communication complexity doesn't indicate consciousness

explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it most accurately states the main purpose of the text. The text first states that animals exhibit complex communication behaviors to share information for various purposes. The text then explains that although scientists used to think only mammals had sophisticated vocal communication, research on prairie dogs (rodents) and honeybees (insects) has shown that mammals are not the only animals with advanced communication systems. Thus, the main purpose of the text is to argue that a variety of animals, not just mammals, have sophisticated communication.
